_source: docs/04 §7 (Names) and §7.1's forty sample outputs. Canon anchor: raw notes name their raiders Bob, Greg and Steve, and docs/04 §7 states the reason the pool looks like this — 'the joke is that this reads like a real guild roster, and canon's own examples are aggressively ordinary. A fantasy name generator would kill the premise on sight.'
_notes: THE CONTENT-REVIEW GATE (docs/04 §7): 'no entry, and no shape-B/C combination of entries, reads as a real identifiable person being mocked. Given names only, no surnames, no full-name pairs, no names of public figures, no names matching anyone on the dev team or in the community.'

Every given name below appears in docs/04 §7.1's own sample table, plus Ron, which §7.1 uses in sample 40 ('Big Ron') without listing separately. Nothing is invented here that the doc did not already print.

Shape C is the risk case the review names: 'an epithet plus a common given name can accidentally land on a real player handle', so the epithet list is deliberately short and every entry is a generic fantasy compound with no real-world referent.

docs/04 §7 asks for `data/names/mundane.txt` and `data/names/epithets.txt`. One JSON file instead, because the shape weights and the mangle rules are data too and splitting them across three files would put one system's tuning in three places. Hot-reloadable either way.

shape_weights._doc: docs/04 §7's table, per-mille so it sums exactly: A 620, B 260, C 120.
